parameters.question: Compare a GRAVY-based protein solubility report. Verify: (1) the original solubility value matches the reference within +/-0.005; (2) the same top 3 single-point mutations (same residue position and substitution) are reported, each with solubility gain matching within +/-0.005; (3) the best mutant sequence matches the reference sequence exactly (character-for-character) and its solubility matches within +/-0.005. Label wording, ordering of fields, and formatting may differ; only the numeric values, mutation identities, and the mutant sequence matter.

Compare two TSV tables reporting GRAVY-based protein solubility predictions for ubiquitin. Each table lists the top 3 single-point mutations substituting a hydrophobic residue with a hydrophilic one, plus the original solubility, the best mutant sequence and its solubility. Align rows by mutation identity (residue position together with the original and substituted amino acid), not by row position, since equal or near-tied solubility gains may be listed in a different order. Column order, header labels (e.g. 'solubility_gain' vs 'gain', 'pos' vs 'position'), residue notation (e.g. 'L8K' vs separate from/to/position columns), and case may differ. Mutation positions and the from/to residues must match the reference. solubility_gain values must agree within +/-0.005; the original solubility and best-mutant solubility must likewise agree within +/-0.005. If a best mutant protein sequence is present, it must match the reference sequence exactly apart from case and line wrapping.
